title: Ctrl+Z stops the foreground job and gives the prompt back; fg resumes it and it reads input again
why: Job control needs the PTY child to be a session leader with a controlling tty (the root cause of the dogfood v1 Ctrl+C bug, fix 66d9960c10f): without it Ctrl+Z sends no SIGTSTP, the shell never gets the terminal back and fg has nothing to resume. The shell reports the reader's state as T (stopped) from ps; the reader prints the upper-case line only if fg resumed it in the foreground and it reads the terminal again. The reader is Python (its reads retry after EINTR, PEP 475), not macOS tr: BSD tr and cat end with 'Interrupted system call' when fg continues them on any macOS PTY (checked on cmux19, macOS 27, with a plain pty.fork and no cmux), so they cannot show the app's job control.

steps.text: python3 -c "import sys; [print(l.upper(), end='', flush=True) for l in sys.stdin]" jr-up

steps.title: the upper-casing reader runs in the foreground of the terminal's tty
the reader answers before the stop
Ctrl+Z stops the reader and the prompt returns

steps.text: echo state-${nonce}-$(ps -o stat=,command= -t $(tty | cut -c6-) | awk '$NF=="jr-up" {print substr($1,1,1)}')

steps.title: the shell takes commands while the reader is stopped, and ps reports it stopped (T)
fg puts the reader back in the foreground
the resumed reader reads the typed line and prints it in upper case
Ctrl+D ends the reader and the prompt returns
